findings.description: The database username and password are rendered into EC2 user data and persisted in /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. This exposes the database secret to principals able to read user data or the instance filesystem.

The RDS instance explicitly sets publicly_accessible = true, allocating a public endpoint even though the shown ingress rule is currently limited to the VPC CIDR. This weakens network segmentation and permits direct public exposure if ingress rules are broadened.
storage_encrypted is explicitly false, leaving RDS database storage and associated automated storage artifacts unencrypted at rest.

The MySQL parameter group does not require secure transport, and the application uses mysqli_connect without TLS configuration. Database credentials and data can therefore be transmitted without encryption between the application and RDS.

MySQL port 3306 is allowed from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application security group or specifically authorized clients. Any workload with an address in that VPC, including a compromised workload, can attempt database connections.

The EC2-attached role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* against every resource. Compromise of the application instance therefore provides broad data-plane and control-plane permissions, including EC2-based privilege-escalation opportunities.
